top_choice_rationale: P001 (Anne Carson) ranks first on the common criteria. Her voice is among the most recognizable on the shortlist: cool, exact, sometimes comic, and able to turn suddenly to grief or desire. Autobiography of Red and Nox, as publicly described, show formal invention serving real emotional and intellectual stakes, and her long engagement with Greek and Latin literature works as method and not decoration. The round 2 exchange narrowed the citation scope, and all four B002 supporters converged on it independently. It credits original written work in English (verse novel, lyric, elegy, essay) and treats translations, adaptations, scholarship and book-object form as context. That answers most of the attribution objection raised by Sem-Sandberg and Mattson. The main unresolved risk is sustained quality: I cannot verify from public knowledge that the mid-career and later books (Eros the Bittersweet, Short Talks, Plainwater, The Beauty of the Husband, Red Doc>, Float) match the two landmarks. P002 (Cărtărescu) is a close second, because his single long project is a serious oeuvre-level case. Whether his recurring imagery is development or repetition cannot be settled from translations, and that uncertainty is not held against him. My ability to read Carson's English directly may inflate my confidence relative to the translated candidates, and I do not count it as merit. I also do not treat the support counts, or the fact that the B002 majority depends on my simulated vote, as literary evidence. P000 is last because both proposals name writers with substantial, distinctive bodies of work, and neither has been shown to fall short of the standard in Nobel's will.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. The profile documents a marriage to a former finance minister, a shared 2020 Academy election with Steve Sem-Sandberg, and working relationships with chair Anders Olsson and predecessor Mats Malm. None of these is a documented connection to Anne Carson, Mircea Cărtărescu or any other shortlisted writer. My own background in literary non-fiction is context only. My simulated vote as a co-opted member is a modeling assumption.
